todayInHistory.title: Fire Causes Significant Damage to Two Harbors Lighthouse Gift Shop
todayInHistory.text: TWO HARBORS, MN – An investigation is underway after a detached building that’s used as a gift shop for the Two Harbors Lighthouse went up in flames Monday evening. As of Tuesday morning, local authorities have yet to release information on the blaze, which likely broke out around 5:30 p.m. Officials with the Lake County Historical Society, which controls the lakeside property, told Northern News Now that no one was injured, but the damage to the building is significant. “We were literally watching a piece of Lake County’s history go up in those flames,” Lake County Historical Society Vice President David Johnson said in an interview with the station. It’s believed that the fire started in the breezeway between the gift shop and a connected structure, both of which are separate from the historic lighthouse. The Lake County Historical Society shared this statement: “We are incredibly grateful to the firefighters and first responders who have responded and are working to address the situation. Their time, dedication, and efforts are greatly appreciated.” Bring Me The News Gift shop fire at Two Harbors Lighthouse.

marineWeather.synopsis: A 29.5 inch trough near the Soo this morning moves east into Quebec and southeast Ontario today. High pressure of 30.2 inches builds in from the northwest tonight through Friday, weakening to 30.1 inches on Saturday as it shifts southeast ahead of a 29.5 inch clipper low crossing Hudson Bay on Sunday.
marineWeather.warning: GALE WARNING IN EFFECT UNTIL 7 PM EST THIS EVENING

marineWeather.synopsis: Low pressure currently at around 29.5 inches will continue to track from eastern Lake Superior through the James Bay Region and into Quebec today. Breezy southwesterly winds with gusts up to 25 knots will persist this morning, before increasing and briefly turning westerly this afternoon as the associated cold front slides across Lake Michigan. Stronger winds then shift to the north-northwest behind the cold front this afternoon/evening. Will see gusts increase to gale force during this time, continuing into Friday as high pressure around 30.3 inches begins to build down across the Upper Midwest. Thus, a Gale Warning remains in effect for these strong winds as they work north to south down Lake Michigan late this afternoon through Friday afternoon. May see gale conditions end sooner for northern portion of Lake Michigan. In addition to the winds, cold air moving into the region Friday paired with warmer Lake temps will result in potential for an isolated waterspout or two for the southeast part of Lake Michigan. High pressure then builds over the Upper Great Lakes overnight Friday through the weekend, bringing lighter northwesterly winds.

AFTERNOON

marineWeather.synopsis: Low pressure, 29.50 inches, over the northern Great Lakes will slowly track into the eastern Great Lakes through tomorrow. Subsequently, A period of strong northeast winds can be expected over Lake Huron on Friday.

Pressure will average 29.80 inches ahead of the next cold front tonight around 29.70 inches into Friday morning. A trough averaging 29.90 inches will linger across the eastern Great Lakes into this weekend. High pressure of 30.10 inches will build into the Ohio Valley Sunday into early next week.

An elongated 29.4 inch low over the central Great Lakes and Ontario will continue to cross into Quebec today and Friday. Following the passage of the low, a 29.9 inch trough will linger across the Lower Great Lakes Saturday. A secondary trough of 29.7 inches will cross the Great Lakes Sunday. A ridge of 30.0 inches will build across the Great Lakes Monday.
